text:
maya: FYI nightly eval threw a weird set of failures on the new prompt normalizer change. ~25 prompts produced truncated model outputs or empty responses. first seen in 03:00 run.
liam: can you paste an example prompt + the normalized result?
maya: example input:
```
User: Summarize the following file:
<file meta>\x00
Content: ... (1000 tokens)
```
normalized -> `User: Summarize the following file:
<file meta>
Content: ...` (notice \x00 removed?)
maya: but the model reply was just `""` (empty) or cut off after first sentence for several cases. attached eval logs: `eval-run-2026-03-19-0300.log` showing 10 timeouts and 15 short outputs.
andre: this is interesting — the normalizer strips non-printables but we also split on NUL to guard against binary blobs. I pushed that change last week. could be colliding with metadata suffixing that teams add.
sophia: also seeing elevated S3 latency during the 03:00 window (S3 GETs for prompt assets spiked to 1.8s). harness has a 2s aggregate read window before starting the run; if prompt fetch delays, we might send an incomplete buffer to the normalizer.
liam: repro steps? I can try a local harness run with slow s3 emulation.
maya: quick repro (attached) — run: `python -m harness.run --prompt-file test_with_null.bin --normalize` results in normalized string truncated at the NUL.
andre: aha — our normalizer currently does `bytes.split(b"\x00")[0]` as a cheap safefilter, which will silently drop anything after the first NUL. If S3 stream is partial and contains a trailing NUL before the rest of the payload arrives, we lose it.
jen: that's scary. two ways to mitigate quickly: 1) revert the normalize-by-nul change in the eval harness; 2) make normalization operate on the full read buffer and only treat embedded NULs as raw bytes to escape instead of split. revert seems fastest for tonight's run.
benchie: I wrote a tiny test case that reproduces the bug deterministically:
```
from io import BytesIO
buf = BytesIO(b"Hello\x00rest_of_prompt")
# current normalizer -> 'Hello' (bad)
# expected -> 'Hello\x00rest_of_prompt' or escape sequence
```
benchie: pushing the unit test to the harness branch now.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: revert/normalize-nul-split -> staging (by jen) :rocket:
oncall: i'm on standby. if we decide to rollback prod branch, ping me.
liam: i'll run the harness with the test-case and s3 latency emulation. if that matches, we can merge the revert and re-run nightly.
maya: note for postmortem — some prompts legitimately contain NULs embedded by downstream ETL, so we need a consistent policy (escape vs strip).
andre: agree. i'll open a design doc for normalization policy. for now i'll PR the escape approach with a feature flag.
sophia: also adding a guard in the runner to refuse to start eval until prompt fetch finishes or to retry partial reads once. that should stop partial-buffer cases.
jen: plan: revert tonight, add unit test (benchie), add S3 read guard (sophia), and design doc for long term (andre). aim to unlock nightly runs by 04:30.
maya: thanks all — i'll annotate the failing evals with repro info and keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
liam: confirmed local repro with latency emu, PR for revert ready.
last: final note: minimal user-facing risk but causes eval noise and false regressions; nice catch by nightly alerts.
